newsitem.title: ISRAEL: ANZ inaugurates East Jerusalem branch.
newsitem.headline: ANZ inaugurates East Jerusalem branch.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand (ANZ) Banking Group inaugurated a branch in Arab East Jerusalem on Wednesday.
Israel's central bank, which licenced the branch, said it hoped the bank would help strengthen ties between Israeli and Asian investors.
An ANZ official in Jerusalem declined to comment on the bank's planned operations, saying a press statement would be issued on Thursday.
ANZ chairman Don Mercer came to Jerusalem for the opening, meeting Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel.

"In the meeting the governor and the chairman of the Australian bank examined the possibility that Israel would become the financial centre of the Middle East," the Bank of Israel said in a statement.
ANZ is the only overseas bank to have a commercial banking licence from Israeli authorities.

"The governor said the Bank of Israel welcomes the direct activities of foreign banks in Israel because it would contribute towards increased competition in the local banking sector and expand the variety of banking services available to the public," the statement added.
The branch was officially opened at a time of high tensions between Israel and the PLO over Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem, which Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war.

Under interim peace deals signed with Israel since 1993, Palestinians have no official say in matters relating to Jerusalem, whose future is to be decided in talks on a permanent peace accord. But the PLO has demanded Israel take no unilateral action to prejudice the outcome of those negotiations.
